site.tagline: Free browser games. No download, no sign-up, no ads before you play.
site.description: spielkunst is a free browser arcade with word games, puzzle games and arcade classics. Play instantly on any device, no install required.

strings.home.title: free browser games, no download
strings.home.lede: Pick a game and you are playing in one second — nothing to install, nothing to unlock, no account.

strings.home.stats.label: The arcade in numbers
strings.home.daily.title: Daily Word Search
strings.home.daily.body: {theme} — {date}. Ten by ten, {count} words, 100 seconds. Everyone plays the same grid.
strings.home.answers.title: Today's answers
strings.home.answers.body: The full solved grid with every word, and a row and column for where each one starts.
strings.home.recent: Pick up where you left off
strings.home.f1.title: Nothing to load first
strings.home.f1.body: Every game is plain JavaScript and canvas. No install, no engine download, no loading bar.
strings.home.f2.title: Nothing to sign up for
strings.home.f2.body: No account, no email, no cookie wall. Your scores and recents stay in your own browser.
strings.home.f3.title: Nothing to pay
strings.home.f3.body: The arcade is funded by labelled sponsor slots, not by interrupting a game you are winning.
strings.home.about1: Every game here runs entirely in your browser. The page is under a megabyte, so it starts instantly on a phone connection, and the daily puzzle archive keeps every past grid so you can look up the answers or replay an old board.
strings.home.about2: {count} of the games are open source, vendored with their original licences and credited on the credits page. The rest are built on the spielkunst engine.
strings.home.slot.title: Your game here
strings.home.slot.body: A labelled sponsor card beside one category of games — an indie game, a dev tool, a newsletter. No pop-ups, ever.

strings.game.howToDefault2: Play with the keyboard, the mouse or touch - the controls are shown in the game.
strings.game.howToDefault3: Score points and try to beat your best run.

strings.index.ledeN: The same arcade, split across {pages} pages so it opens fast. Search reaches all {count} games, whichever page they live on.
strings.index.emptyBody: Try a shorter word, or clear the filter.
strings.credits.title: Credits — the games and people behind {site}
strings.credits.desc: Credits for {site}: original games by Ayhem Kahri plus open-source games by Nicky Case, Jake Gordon and mumuy, with licences and source links.
strings.credits.intro: {site} is built by Ayhem Kahri. Some games are original; the rest are open-source projects by other people, vendored here with their original licences and a link back to the source.
strings.credits.originalBody: Written for {site}, running on a custom TypeScript engine with no third-party runtime dependencies.
strings.credits.ossBody: Each of these is the author's original work, vendored under its own licence. The full licence text ships inside each game's folder.
strings.credits.thanksBody: Nicky Case for Trust and Loopy, Jake Gordon for Javascript Tetris, and mumuy for Pacman. Their work made this collection what it is.
strings.daily.title: Daily Word Search archive — every puzzle and answer
strings.daily.desc: Play or look up every daily word search puzzle. A new free 10x10 grid every day with the full answer list for each one.
strings.daily.intro: One new 10x10 word search every day. Everyone plays the same grid, so you can compare scores with friends or look back at a puzzle you missed.
strings.daily.howBody: The grid is generated from the date, which means every player gets exactly the same board at the same time. Drag across a straight line of letters to select a word — horizontally, vertically or diagonally. You have 100 seconds.
strings.daily.puzzle.title: Daily Word Search {date} — free puzzle and answers
strings.daily.puzzle.desc: Free daily word search for {date}. {theme} theme, {count} hidden words, 100 seconds to find them. Same grid for every player.
strings.daily.puzzle.lede: Free daily word search puzzle for {date}. 10x10 grid, {count} hidden words, 100 seconds on the clock. The same grid for every player.
strings.daily.stuck: {count} words are hidden in this grid. If you are stuck, the answer page for {date} lists every word and where it starts and ends.
strings.daily.howPlay1: Drag across a straight line of letters — horizontal, vertical or diagonal.
strings.daily.howPlay2: Release to submit. Correct words stay highlighted.
strings.daily.howPlay3: 100 seconds. Longer words and faster finds score more.
strings.daily.answersDesc: Full answer list for the {date} daily word search: {words}. Solved grid and start/end positions for every word.
strings.daily.answers.lede: Every word hidden in the {date} puzzle, with the row and column where each one starts and ends. {count} words in total.
strings.daily.aboutBody: This puzzle was generated on {date} using the {theme} word list. Every player gets the same grid, and a new one appears every day at midnight UTC. Play it free on {site} or browse the full archive.
strings.ad.title: Advertise — sponsor a slot in the arcade
strings.ad.desc: Put your game, tool or newsletter in front of {site} players: one labelled sponsor slot per category, no pop-ups, from $5. Sponsors only — no ad networks.
strings.ad.h1: Put your thing in the cabinet.
strings.ad.intro: spielkunst is a free arcade with a daily puzzle that brings people back every day. A few quiet, labelled sponsor slots are what keep it free — and one of them can be yours.
strings.ad.whatBody: A text (or small image) card, always marked Sponsored, shown beside the games of one category and on that category's hub pages. One sponsor per category — a player sees yours, and only yours.
strings.ad.rule1: No pop-ups, interstitials, auto-playing sound or floating panels — those would kill an arcade like this.
strings.ad.rule2: Never mixed into game results, scores or the puzzle grid.
strings.ad.rule3: No tracking scripts at any price.
strings.ad.whatFoot: What you buy is placement, not scale: traffic here is real, small, and growing through the daily puzzle. Prices match that.
strings.ad.row1.name: Launch week
strings.ad.row1.where: Any slot, one week, first month only
strings.ad.row2.name: Category slot
strings.ad.row3.name: Site-wide slot
strings.ad.flat: Flat. No impressions, no bidding, no renewals held hostage — cancel any month.
strings.ad.start1: Write to me with your name, what you advertise and the link.
strings.ad.start2: Your slot goes live on the next build — usually the same day — and you see it on the real site before paying anything.
strings.ad.start3: You get an invoice (bank transfer or Payoneer) after the slot is live — you only pay once it is on the site.
strings.ad.fitsBody: Games, game-dev tools, word-game and puzzle books, education, indie newsletters. Family-friendly only: no gambling, no crypto, no loot boxes, nothing you couldn't explain to a nine-year-old.
strings.ad.contactBody: One line is enough to start:

strings.nf.desc: That page does not exist on {site}.
strings.nf.h1: That page is not in the cabinet.
strings.nf.body: It may have moved, or it never existed. The games all still work — pick one, or go back to the start.

word.title: Word Games
word.description: Word puzzles you can play in under a minute. New challenges every day.

puzzle.title: Puzzle Games
puzzle.description: Logic and number puzzles with instant restart and no waiting.

arcade.title: Arcade Games
arcade.description: Classic arcade action, rebuilt for the browser and playable on a phone.

brain.title: Brain Games
brain.description: Memory, attention and pattern games that train while you play.

strategy.title: Strategy Games
strategy.description: Games about decisions, trust and systems. Think it through before you play.

sandbox.title: Sandbox & Tools
sandbox.description: Open-ended toys for playing with ideas. No score, no timer, just make something.

classics.title: Classics
classics.description: Pong, Breakout, Space Invaders and the cabinets they came from. Same rules, no quarters.

racing.title: Racing Games
racing.description: Top-down and side-scrolling racers you can steer with two thumbs.

table.title: Table Games
table.description: Board and card games with no setup: sudoku, solitaire, mahjong, ludo, go.

2048.tagline: Slide, merge and build the biggest number.
2048.description: Slide the whole board with each move, merge matching numbers and build the largest tile you can.
howToPlay: Slide every tile with the arrow keys, or use the on-screen pad.
Two tiles with the same number merge into one when they meet.
Swipe on a phone to send the whole board that way.

faq.a: When the board is full and no two neighbours match. Until then, every swipe has somewhere to go.
Keep the largest tile in one corner and build in a single direction, so the board never needs rearranging.

snake.tagline: Eat, grow longer and keep clear of your own tail.
snake.description: Steer a snake around the board, eat what spawns and avoid your own tail as the body gets longer.
howToPlay: Steer with the arrow keys, or use the on-screen pad.
Swipe on a phone to send the snake a new direction.
Eat the food, grow longer and never touch the walls or your own tail.

faq.a: Hitting a wall or your own tail. In most versions the walls do not wrap, so the edge of the board is the end.
The snake speeds up and takes up more of the board as it grows, so the turns come sooner and leave less room.

tetris.tagline: Stack the falling blocks and clear every line.
tetris.description: Drop the falling blocks into place, fill a full row across the board and keep the stack away from the top.
howToPlay: Move with the left and right arrows, rotate with the up arrow.
Soft-drop with the down arrow and hard-drop with Space.
Fill a whole row across the board to clear it and keep the stack low.

faq.q: What happens when the stack reaches the top?
faq.a: The round ends. Clearing a row buys the height back, so keep the left and right edges low.

faq.q: Does clearing four rows at once score more?
faq.a: In most versions it does, and by more than four single rows. Saving a well for a long piece is worth the wait.

pong.tagline: Keep the ball in play and return every shot.
pong.description: Move your paddle to meet every shot, angle the ball past your opponent and take the point.
howToPlay: Move your paddle with the up and down arrows, or use the on-screen pad.
Swipe up or down on a phone to move the paddle.
Return the ball past your opponent to win the point.

faq.a: Return the ball past your opponent's paddle. The first side to reach the target score takes the match.

faq.q: Can I play against a person?
faq.a: In most versions the far paddle is the computer. Some of them also offer two players on the same keyboard.

pacman.tagline: Clear the maze while the ghosts hunt you down.
pacman.description: Run the maze, eat every dot along the way and slip past the ghosts before they close in.
howToPlay: Move with the arrow keys, or use the on-screen pad.
Swipe on a phone to turn at the next corner.
Eat every dot in the maze and keep away from the ghosts.

faq.q: What do the big dots do?
faq.a: They turn the ghosts around for a few seconds, and a ghost caught in that time goes back to its corner.

faq.q: Is there a way out of the maze?
faq.a: Clear every dot on the board. In most versions a fresh maze follows, with ghosts that move a little faster.

breakout.tagline: Bounce the ball, break the wall and keep the paddle ready.
breakout.description: Slide the paddle, bounce the ball into the bricks and clear the whole wall without losing the ball.
howToPlay: Slide the paddle with the left and right arrows, or use the on-screen pad.
Bounce the ball into the bricks without letting it past you.
Clear every brick to finish the wall and move on.

faq.q: What happens when I miss the ball?
faq.a: You lose a life and the ball starts again from the paddle. Most versions give you three lives.

faq.q: Can I control where the ball goes?
faq.a: Partly. The ball leaves the paddle at an angle set by where it struck, so the edges of the paddle send it wider.

invaders.tagline: Hold the line and clear the sky, wave after wave.
invaders.description: Hold the line at the bottom of the screen, fire upwards and clear each formation before it lands.
howToPlay: Move with the left and right arrows, or use the on-screen pad.
Fire with Space or the A button on the pad.
Clear each wave before it reaches the bottom of the screen.

faq.q: Why do the invaders speed up?
faq.a: The fewer that are left, the faster the rest move, so the last few are the hardest to hit.

faq.q: What happens if they reach the bottom?
faq.a: The round ends. Keep the nearest row clear and work from the edges inwards.

racing.tagline: Steer for the line and keep your foot down.
racing.description: Steer through the course, brake into the corners and hold your line all the way to the flag.
howToPlay: Steer with the left and right arrows, or use the on-screen pad.
Accelerate with the up arrow and brake with the down arrow.
Swipe left or right on a phone to steer through the corner.

faq.q: Do I have to finish first?
faq.a: No. Learn the corners at your own pace and the lap times come down on their own.

faq.q: What is the quickest way round a corner?
faq.a: Brake before the turn rather than in it, then accelerate out once the car is pointing the right way.

platformer.tagline: Run, jump and reach the end of the level.
platformer.description: Run along the level, jump the gaps and time each leap so you land on solid ground.
howToPlay: Move with the left and right arrows, or use the on-screen pad.
Jump with Space or the up arrow.
Swipe up on a phone to jump, and swipe left or right to run.

faq.q: How do I know how far I can jump?
faq.a: Watch the gap rather than the character. If it is wider than the last one you cleared, jump from the very edge.
In most versions you restart from the last checkpoint, or from the start of the level if there is none.

flappy.tagline: Tap to flap and thread every gap.
flappy.description: Tap to keep the bird in the air, thread every gap and see how far one run will take you.
howToPlay: Tap the screen or press Space to flap.
Pass through each gap without touching the edges.
Press R to start again after a crash.

faq.a: Too many taps. Short taps hold your height, long presses climb, and the bird keeps whatever speed you gave it.
No. The gaps keep coming and the run stops at the first crash, so the score is simply how far you got.

maze.tagline: Find the way out before the walls close in.
maze.description: Find the route through the walls, remember the dead ends and make your way to the exit.
howToPlay: Move with the arrow keys, or use the on-screen pad.
Swipe on a phone to turn at the next junction.
Reach the way out without getting stuck in a dead end.

faq.a: Most mazes can be solved from any point. Follow one wall and you will reach either the exit or the start again.
In most versions, yes. The clock is the pressure, so keep moving rather than studying the whole map first.

match3.tagline: Swap two tiles and line up three.
match3.description: Swap two neighbouring tiles, line up three of a colour and clear them to open up the board.
howToPlay: Pick a tile with a tap or a click, then pick the one next to it.
Line up three or more of the same colour to clear them.
Move the selection with the arrow keys or the on-screen pad.

faq.a: Three or more of the same colour in a row, across or down. Longer runs clear more of the board at once.
The tiles above fall into the gap and new ones come in at the top, which can set up a second match for free.

sliding.tagline: Slide the tiles into order, one move at a time.
sliding.description: Move one tile at a time into the empty space and put the whole picture back in order.
howToPlay: Move a tile into the empty space with the arrow keys.
Swipe on a phone to slide the tile in that direction.
Put every tile back in order to finish the puzzle.

faq.a: Not every one. Half of the arrangements cannot be reached from the finished puzzle, and the game deals you one that can.

faq.q: How many moves does it take?
faq.a: A good solve takes about eighty moves from a shuffle. The count on screen tells you how you are doing.

sokoban.tagline: Push every crate into place without getting stuck.
sokoban.description: Walk the room, push each crate onto its mark and take care never to trap it against a wall.
howToPlay: Move with the arrow keys, or use the on-screen pad.
Walk into a crate to push it one square.
Swipe on a phone to push the crate in that direction.

faq.a: No, you can only push. That is why a crate against a wall can be lost, so plan the last push before the first.

faq.q: How do I undo a mistake?
faq.a: Most versions have an undo or a restart. Use it early, because a single wrong push can cost the whole level.

memory.tagline: Turn two cards, remember where they were, find the pairs.
memory.description: Turn two cards at a time, remember where each picture sits and pair up the whole board.
howToPlay: Pick a card with a tap or a click to turn it over.
Turn a second card and keep the pair when the two match.
Move the selection with the arrow keys or the on-screen pad.

faq.q: Does it matter which card I turn first?
faq.a: Not for the rules, but it helps your memory. Turn an unknown card first and a card you remember second.
By how few turns it takes to clear the board. Fewer turns mean a better memory, not a faster click.

sudoku.tagline: Fill the grid so every row, column and box is complete.
sudoku.description: Fill every row, column and box with the digits one to nine, each of them used exactly once.
howToPlay: Pick a square with a tap or a click, then choose the number you want.
Move between squares with the arrow keys or the on-screen pad.
Every row, column and box must hold each number exactly once.

faq.a: A well-made puzzle never needs a guess. If two numbers both fit a square, one of them breaks a row further along.
Each of the nine small boxes holds one to nine exactly once, the same as every row and every column.

solitaire.tagline: Build the four suits from ace to king.
solitaire.description: Deal the cards, build each suit from ace to king and turn over the hidden cards as you go.
howToPlay: Pick up a card with a tap or a click, then pick the pile it belongs on.
Move the selection with the arrow keys or the on-screen pad.
Build each suit in order and turn over the hidden cards as you go.

faq.q: What can I move onto a column?
faq.a: A card one rank lower and of the opposite colour. An empty column will take any card or any run.

faq.q: What if no move is left?
faq.a: Turn the stock again if the version allows it. Most deals can be won, but not every one of them can.

mahjong.tagline: Clear the board by pairing matching tiles.
mahjong.description: Pair identical tiles from the edges and work inwards until the whole board has been cleared.
howToPlay: Pick two matching tiles with a tap or a click.
Move the selection with the arrow keys or the on-screen pad.
Only tiles with a free side can be taken, so work inwards from the edges.

faq.q: Why can I not take that tile?
faq.a: A tile needs a free left or right side. Tiles boxed in at both ends stay locked until the board opens up.
Most are, but the order matters. If a pair leaves two tiles stranded, undo it and try the other pair first.

hangman.tagline: Guess the hidden word before the picture is complete.
hangman.description: Guess the hidden word one letter at a time and keep your wrong guesses down to a handful.
howToPlay: Choose a letter with a tap or a click.
Move between letters with the arrow keys or the on-screen pad.
Six wrong guesses end the round, so start with the common letters.

faq.q: How many wrong guesses do I get?
faq.a: Six in most versions. Vowels first is a good habit, then the consonants that turn up in everything.

faq.q: Does a repeated letter count twice?
faq.a: No. A letter is one guess however many times it appears, so long words are often easier than short ones.

wordsearch.tagline: Find every hidden word in the grid.
wordsearch.description: Scan the grid across, down and diagonally to find every word on the list before the round ends.
howToPlay: Drag across a line of letters, or move the cursor with the arrow keys.
Words can run across, down, up or diagonally.
Mark every word on the list to finish the puzzle.

faq.a: Across, down and diagonally, forwards and backwards in most grids. Keep an eye on the list as you go.

faq.q: What happens if I mark the wrong line?
faq.a: Nothing. The selection clears and the grid stays as it was, so there is no cost to trying a line.

wordle.tagline: Six guesses to find the five-letter word.
wordle.description: Guess the five-letter word in six tries, using the colour clues after each attempt to narrow it down.
howToPlay: Type a word, or pick the letters on the keyboard shown in the game.
Green means the right letter in the right place; yellow means it belongs elsewhere.
Press Enter or the B button on the pad to submit your guess.

faq.a: Green is the right letter in the right place. Yellow is a letter that belongs in the word but somewhere else.

faq.q: Can I guess the same word twice?
faq.a: You can, but it wastes a row. Every guess has to be a real word, so there is no way to test letters in bulk.

quiz.tagline: Answer the questions and see how much you know.
quiz.description: Answer a run of questions, pick from the choices on screen and see how many you get right.
howToPlay: Pick an answer with a tap or a click.
Move between answers with the arrow keys or the on-screen pad.
Every correct answer adds to your score, and the questions keep coming.

faq.a: In most versions each question has one. Answer the ones you know first and come back to the rest if you can.
Usually at the end of the run. The score is the point, so most quizzes hold the answers back until then.

typing.tagline: Type the words as fast and as accurately as you can.
typing.description: Type each word that appears as quickly and as accurately as you can, and keep the run going.
howToPlay: Type each word that appears, then press Space to move on.
Keep your hands on the keyboard and your eyes on the text.
Accuracy and speed both count towards your score.

faq.q: Which matters more, speed or accuracy?
faq.a: Accuracy. A wrong letter costs more time than a slow one, because fixing it costs another keystroke.

faq.q: Should I look at the keyboard?
faq.a: No. Keep your eyes on the text and let your fingers learn the keys, even if the first few runs are slow.

towerdefense.tagline: Build your towers and hold the line against the waves.
towerdefense.description: Place towers along the path, spend what you earn on upgrades and stop every wave before it reaches the base.
howToPlay: Pick a tower with a tap or a click, then pick a spot beside the path.
Move between build spots with the arrow keys or the on-screen pad.
Each wave is stronger than the last, so upgrade before it arrives.

faq.a: At the bends. A tower covers more of the path where it turns, so a corner is worth two straight stretches.
Upgrade the towers on the busiest stretch first. A few strong towers usually beat a long line of weak ones.

roguelike.tagline: One life, a fresh dungeon and a fight to the last floor.
roguelike.description: Take one life into a fresh dungeon, fight what you meet and see how deep you can get.
howToPlay: Move one square at a time with the arrow keys, or use the on-screen pad.
Walk into a monster to attack it and step on an item to pick it up.
Swipe on a phone to move one square at a time.

faq.a: Usually not. One life is the point of the genre, so the run ends with you and the next dungeon is new.
No. Experience is useful, but a fight you can walk away from is a fight you cannot lose.

shooter.tagline: Keep moving, keep firing and stay alive.
shooter.description: Keep moving, aim at whatever comes for you and clear the screen without taking a hit.
howToPlay: Move with the arrow keys, or use the on-screen pad.
Fire with Space or the A button on the pad.
Dodge what comes at you and clear the screen.

faq.a: Standing still makes you an easy target. Most of these games aim where you are, so a step sideways is a dodge.

faq.q: What is the best way to clear a wave?
faq.a: Work from the outside in and leave yourself a way out, rather than backing into a corner.

idle.tagline: Start small, earn steadily and watch the numbers grow.
idle.description: Tap to earn your first coins, spend them on upgrades and watch the numbers climb while you wait.
howToPlay: Tap or click to earn your first coins.
Spend what you earn on upgrades that earn faster.
Move between upgrades with the arrow keys or the on-screen pad.

faq.q: Do I have to keep the page open?
faq.a: Usually yes, though many of these games keep earning while the tab sits in the background.
The upgrade with the shortest payback. Work out how long it takes to earn its cost back before you spend.

board.tagline: Take turns, think ahead and win the board.
board.description: Take turns moving your pieces, plan a few moves ahead and protect your own side of the board.
howToPlay: Pick a piece with a tap or a click, then pick where it moves.
Move the selection with the arrow keys or the on-screen pad.
Take turns with your opponent and protect your own pieces.

faq.a: In most versions the other side is the computer. Some of them also offer two players on one screen.

faq.q: Is there a time limit per turn?
faq.a: Sometimes. Where there is one, the clock sits next to your name and the turn passes when it runs out.

generic.tagline: A quick game to pick up and play in the browser.
generic.description: Read the prompts, pick up the controls as you go and see how far one run of this browser game takes you.
howToPlay: Tap or click to start, then follow the prompts inside the game.
Move with the arrow keys, or use the on-screen pad.
Swipe on a phone to send the arrow keys the game expects.

faq.a: Tap or click the game once and follow the prompt it shows. Most of these games start on the first input.

faq.q: What if the controls do not respond?
faq.a: Click the game area once to give it focus, then try again. Keys only reach the game while it has focus.
